messages:
maria: heads up — ran into a production case where a service had only an org-scoped token and our router fell back to a project pool; this caused surprising permission mismatches. thinking we need a clear fallthrough policy for tokens that don't map cleanly to a project. opinions? :thinking:

kevin: ugh, yeah i've seen that. current behavior is effectively permissive: org-key -> best-effort project routing if affinity exists. that was pragmatic but risky for least-privilege guarantees.

sophia: imo we should default to strict (deny; explicit mapping required). falling back silently leaks surface area. but we need a migration/compat path for older tokens.

raj: +1 on strict by default. also: telemetry hooks and a "warn" mode are critical so teams can see failures before we flip to hard deny. we should expose a flag: `auth.fallthrough = strict|warn|permissive` and make it configurable per-environment.

carla: quick pseudo-resolution order idea:
```
# resolution order (router)
if token.scope == 'project':
  route -> project pool
elif token.scope == 'org' and token.binding.project_id != null:
  route -> bound project pool (explicit bind)
elif token.scope == 'org' and tenant_affinity.exists(token.org_id, target_service):
  if config.auth.fallthrough == 'permissive':
    route -> inferred project pool (audit)
  elif config.auth.fallthrough == 'warn':
    log.warn('org->project fallthrough', token.id, hint)
    route -> inferred project pool
  else:
    reject 401 'insufficient scope'
else:
  reject 401 'no project scope'
```

kevin: that looks reasonable. i'd add an allowlist for legacy workloads that can't be migrated yet (tenant-migration.allowlist = [svcA, svcB]) so we don't block critical jobs. allowlist should be temporary + audited.

maria: sounds like three levers then: strict deny, warn (soft rollback), permissive (compat + audit). who owns rolling this out? i'd like a canary: start `warn` for 2 weeks in staging -> `warn` in prod a subset -> strict after migration window. :chart_with_upwards_trend:

sophia: i'll take docs + SDK changes for the new 401 error codes and the `auth.fallthrough` config. will add examples for server-side SDKs showing how to detect fallthrough rejects and surface migration guidance.

raj: migration plan sketch: 1) enable `warn` in staging for 2w, collect telemetry + top offenders; 2) open migration tickets per owning team; 3) offer short-lived project-scoped tokens as a fast workaround; 4) after 8w flip to `strict` except allowlist; 5) wipe allowlist after 12w.

maria: +1. we should also add a runtime metric `auth.fallthrough.attempts` tagged by org, service, and route so SRE/product can prioritize.

auth-bot: CI: policy-auth-fallthrough branch merged to staging, tests passing — deploy scheduled 03:15 UTC. :deploy:

carla: small note — router logs need a consistent reason string for rejections so observability and error pages can show helpful next steps (e.g., "REJECT_SCOPE_MISSING -> ask infra to mint project token").

kevin: agree. propose error codes: `REJECT_SCOPE_MISSING`, `REJECT_SCOPE_MISMATCH`, `FALLTHROUGH_AUDIT` for warn/permissive path.

maria: ok actionable items: kevin will draft a short RFC with the state machine + config + error codes; sophia will update SDK docs and error handling examples; raj will own telemetry + rollout plan; carla will add router pseudocode + tests. i'll schedule a 30m sync on monday to review the RFC. thanks all. :thumbsup:

kevin: i'll aim to post the RFC by EOD tomorrow.

sophia: noted, i'll prep docs PR after the RFC so wording matches.

raj: i'll stub dashboards and alert queries, linking to the RFC when ready.

maria: perfect — we'll include rollback knobs in the deploy and an oncall runbook for unexpected breakage.

kevin: one more thought — consider a migration helper endpoint `POST /auth/migrate-token` that exchanges an org token for a scoped short-lived project token after owner consent. could reduce friction.

sophia: nice. adds UX but worth it. i'll add to docs if we include it.

maria: great idea, add it to the RFC. closing note: keep the default strict and promote warn/permissive only as temporary migration modes with clear telemetry.

carla: ack. i'll add unit tests for the three-mode behavior and include samples in the RFC.

maria: thanks everyone — RFC + sync next week.
